sources.note: Classification: Unclassifiable; AES status 10 (Extinct); NOCODE; zero bibliographic references listed.

Describes it as an extinct Northern Iroquoian language 'mutually intelligible with the Wendat language' (unsourced beyond Julian 2010); no vocabulary or grammatical data; only source cited is Julian 2010 for the ethnonym etymology.

sources.citation: Julian, Charles (2010). A History of the Iroquoian Languages. PhD thesis, University of Manitoba, Winnipeg. Section 18.3 'Wenro', pp. 336-337 (intro to ch. 18 p. 335).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Wenro is listed among the 'fragmentary (or altogether unattested) Northern Iroquoian languages' (p. 335); the Wenro section (pp. 336-337) is purely ethnohistorical: the only linguistic material is the Huron exonym <8enro'ronon>/<Ahouenrochrhonon> and the village name/ethnonym <Ouaroronon> recorded by La Roche Daillon in 1627. No Wenro words, phonology, or stress.

sources.citation: White, Marian (1978). 'Neutral and Wenro'. In Handbook of North American Indians vol. 15 (Northeast), pp. 407-411; and Hewitt, J.N.B. (1912) 'Wenrohronon', Handbook of American Indians North of Mexico, p. 933 — seen only as cited in Julian 2010
